subtitle: Lesson 22 · Teleportation & Superdense Coding in Practice

steps.label: No unitary U can take an unknown |ψ⟩ and copy it
steps.sub: No U, no fixed ancilla, that produces two independent |ψ⟩'s for every input

steps.label: Follows directly from linearity
steps.sub: Not an engineering limit — a mathematical contradiction if it existed

steps.label: It forbids copying an UNKNOWN state
steps.sub: Preparing known states, like extra |0⟩'s, is never restricted

steps.label: Before: exactly one copy of |ψ⟩, on Alice's q1
steps.sub: Nothing exists yet on Bob's side

steps.label: During: entangling gates spread correlation, not copies
steps.sub: No point has "|ψ⟩ here AND |ψ⟩ there"

steps.label: Measurement destroys the original on Alice's side
steps.sub: Her superposition is gone permanently the instant she measures

steps.label: After correction: exactly one copy, now on Bob's q3
steps.sub: The state relocated — it never duplicated

eyebrow: The other half of the argument

steps.label: Superdense coding never copies an unknown state
steps.sub: Alice sends one of 4 choices SHE fully knows and controls

steps.label: Bob's qubit looks maximally mixed before the bits arrive
steps.sub: Informationless — no way to detect anything happened

steps.label: Entanglement sets up correlation, not communication
steps.sub: Turning it into a usable result needs the classical message

steps.label: That message is bound by the normal speed-of-light limit
steps.sub: Causality is never at risk in either protocol
